transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining today's planning meeting. As you know, we've recently combined two groups in the department, and leadership has agreed to create a staff listening council to address concerns about the new working relationships. The council will meet monthly for its first several meetings and will provide a written summary to me. Before I sign off on the plan, I'd like to hear from each of you about how you think the council should be designed — its membership, operating format, and any safeguards you'd recommend. Let's go around the room in our usual round-robin format. Each of you, please share your recommendation, note any action that comes out of it, and identify who would be responsible for that action. Who would like to start?

I've personally observed four tense exchanges where employees stopped speaking the moment their direct manager joined the discussion. Two of the affected employees specifically asked me not to put them in a manager-led forum. I haven't raised this with Priya until now because those employees did not want the issue escalated through their managers. transcript.text: Thank you, Noor. I'll go next with my recommendation. Based on what I've observed — employees going silent when managers join discussions and two employees explicitly asking not to be in a manager-led forum — I want to recommend specific safeguards that go beyond just excluding supervisors as observers. For membership, I agree with Noor's recommendation for non-managerial staff representatives from both combined groups, and I'd add that membership should include at least one representative from each of the two former groups to ensure both sides of the newly combined workforce have a voice. For operating format, I recommend that the council designate a specific point of contact who is outside the direct reporting chain — someone employees can approach privately before or between meetings if they have concerns they're not comfortable raising in the group setting. This addresses the pattern I saw where people shut down in real-time when managers appeared. For safeguards, I recommend two things: first, that the anonymous written question channel Maya referenced be structured so that questions cannot be traced back to individual employees through metadata or submission logs — true anonymity, not just confidentiality. Second, that the council establish a clear protocol where any manager attendance is pre-announced to members at least 48 hours in advance, so no employee is caught off guard by a manager's presence and forced to choose between speaking up and staying silent in the moment. As for actions: first, draft a protocol for pre-announcing any manager attendance at council meetings with 48 hours' notice — I'll take responsibility for that. Second, designate a point of contact outside the direct reporting chain for private employee concerns between meetings — I'd recommend this be assigned to someone Priya appoints, since it needs to be someone all employees trust. I'll note that as an action for Priya to assign.
